title: Flexible product attributes with jsonb
scenario: Phones need RAM and storage, shoes need size and colour; the products table has grown to 140 nullable columns.
stack: Spring Boot 4.1.1 · Java 25 · JdbcClient · PostgreSQL 17 jsonb · containment (@>) · GIN jsonb_path_ops · rules as data · Testcontainers
simulation: Sellers, categories and products are demo data (60,006 products), not Kartwala's. Nothing is sold.

tabs.html:
Belongs in this tab

  • The real-life problem as a 3-step story
  • What we are building, and an everyday analogy
  • How it works in 4 steps
  • One question to check yourself
  • What this station is not
  • Key terms

Level 1, about 5 minutes. Plain language: no code.

The problem in real life

  1. 140 columns

    Phones need RAM and storage, shoes need size and colour, sarees need fabric. Each new category added columns that are empty for every other product.

  2. Everything in JSON

    The first fix put the whole product in one jsonb column. A seller typed "free" as the price, and every customer's price filter failed. Duplicate SKUs and unknown sellers got in too.

  3. The fix

    Columns for what every product has and the rules it needs; jsonb only for what differs per category, checked against that category's rules.

Flexible data still needs rules. Keep the rules close to the data.

What are we building?

POST /products adds a product with its category's attributes, checked; GET /products?attr.ram=8GB finds products by any mix of attributes, through an index.

An everyday analogy

A registration form: printed boxes everyone fills (name, price, seller), and a page of extra questions that depends on what you register: a phone asks for RAM, a shoe for size. The clerk checks the extra page against that type's list.

How it works in 4 steps

  1. Check the printed boxes: SKU, name, price range, seller.
  2. Load the category's rules and check the attributes: known names, allowed values, nothing required missing.
  3. Store the fixed fields in columns, the attributes as one jsonb object.
  4. Search with "the attributes contain these pairs", answered by the GIN index.
Check yourself: should "brand" be a column or an attribute?

If every product has a brand, people filter and sort by it, and brands are their own table you join to, it is a column with a foreign key. If only some categories have it and it is just shown, an attribute is fine. The test is the one in this station: does it need a constraint or a join?

What this station is not

  • No admin screen for rules. Rules are rows; Practice 1 reads them.
  • No numeric ranges on attributes. Values are text; "RAM at least 8GB" needs typed attributes.
  • No document database. That is station 070.

Key terms

AttributeA property that only some products have.RAM for a phone, size for a shoe.attributes

Level 2. What a teammate hands you before you build.

Business problem

Kartwala (a fictional marketplace) has a products table with 140 nullable columns, one set per category.

Acceptance criteria

Demo data: phones need ram and storage (colour optional); shoes need size and colour (material optional).

  1. Given a phone with ram, storage and colour, then 201 with the attributes stored.
  2. Given a shoe of size 13 with ram and no colour, then 422 naming each problem.
  3. Given an unknown category or seller, then 422; a duplicate SKU, 409.
  4. Given attr.ram=8GB&attr.storage=256GB, then only products with both.
  5. Given an attribute no category has (or not this category), then 400.
  6. Given any search, then the GIN index is used.

Requirements

  • Price, seller, category and SKU are columns with constraints.
  • Attributes are a jsonb object, checked against the category's rules before saving.
  • A new category or attribute is a row in attribute_definitions, not a release.
  • Searches use containment, which the GIN index answers.

Learning objectives

  • Store and query jsonb from Java.
  • Index jsonb with GIN and know which operators use it.
  • Validate per-category attributes from data.
  • Decide what is a column and what is an attribute.

CaseWhat happensProved by

The trap

Plausible but wrong

Putting everything in jsonb, including fields that need constraints and joins.

The test builds the old table: one data column per product, price and seller inside. Then:

  • Anything gets in. A second PH-NOVA-8-128, a price of "free", seller 999, RAM "lots": all accepted. There is nothing to attach a constraint to.
  • One bad row breaks everyone. (data->>'price')::int < 200000 worked, until the "free" row: then it fails for every customer with "invalid input syntax for type integer: "free"".
  • The real table refuses the same rows: products_sku_unique, products_price_range, products_seller_fk.
  • The index only helps the right operator. attributes @> '{"ram": "12GB"}' uses the GIN index; attributes->>'ram' = '12GB' reads every row.

package com.kartwala.attributes;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.AfterEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.dao.DataAccessException;

import java.util.Map;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

/**
 * Written first. The old table kept the whole product in one jsonb column, price and seller included, on a copy of
 * the demo catalog. Then the same mistakes against the real table.
 */
class EverythingInJsonbTrapTest extends ApiTest {

    @BeforeEach
    void oldTable() {
        jdbc.sql("CREATE TABLE old_products (id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, data JSONB NOT NULL)").update();
        jdbc.sql("""
                INSERT INTO old_products (data) SELECT jsonb_build_object('sku', sku, 'name', name, 'category', category_code,
                    'seller', seller_id, 'price', price_paise) || attributes FROM products""").update();
    }

    @AfterEach
    void dropOldTable() {
        jdbc.sql("DROP TABLE old_products").update();
    }

    @Test
    void anythingGetsIntoTheOldTable() {
        jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO old_products (data) VALUES ('{\"sku\": \"PH-NOVA-8-128\", \"price\": \"free\", \"seller\": 999, \"ram\": \"lots\"}')").update();
        assertThat(jdbc.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM old_products WHERE data->>'sku' = 'PH-NOVA-8-128'").query(Long.class).single()).isEqualTo(2);   // a duplicate SKU
    }

    @Test
    void oneBadPriceBreaksEveryPriceQuery() {
        String under2000 = "SELECT count(*) FROM old_products WHERE (data->>'price')::int < 200000";
        assertThat(jdbc.sql(under2000).query(Long.class).single()).isPositive();
        jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO old_products (data) VALUES ('{\"sku\": \"T-ODD\", \"price\": \"free\"}')").update();
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> jdbc.sql(under2000).query(Long.class).single()).rootCause()
                .hasMessageContaining("invalid input syntax for type integer: \"free\"");   // every customer's price filter now fails
    }

    @Test
    void theRealTableRefusesTheSameRows() {
        String insert = "INSERT INTO products (sku, name, category_code, seller_id, price_paise, attributes) VALUES (?, 'X', 'phones', ?, ?, '{}')";
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> jdbc.sql(insert).params("PH-NOVA-8-128", 7, 100000).update()).isInstanceOf(DataAccessException.class).hasMessageContaining("products_sku_unique");
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> jdbc.sql(insert).params("T-FREE", 7, 0).update()).hasMessageContaining("products_price_range");
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> jdbc.sql(insert).params("T-NOBODY", 999, 100000).update()).hasMessageContaining("products_seller_fk");
    }

    @Test
    void containmentUsesTheGinIndexTheArrowOperatorDoesNot() {
        assertThat(indexesUsed("SELECT id FROM products WHERE attributes @> CAST(:wanted AS jsonb)", Map.of("wanted", "{\"ram\": \"12GB\"}")))
                .containsExactly("products_attributes");
        assertThat(indexesUsed("SELECT id FROM products WHERE attributes->>'ram' = :ram", Map.of("ram", "12GB"))).isEmpty();
    }
}

    @GetMapping("/products")
    List<ProductCatalog.Product> search(@RequestParam Map<String, String> params) {
        Map<String, String> wanted = new TreeMap<>();
        params.forEach((key, value) -> {
            if (key.startsWith("attr.")) {
                wanted.put(key.substring(5), value);
            } else if (!key.equals("category")) {

            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "Give 1 to 10 attr.<name>=<value> filters");

Why

package com.kartwala.attributes;

import org.springframework.dao.DataIntegrityViolationException;
import org.springframework.dao.DuplicateKeyException;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.jdbc.core.simple.JdbcClient;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;
import org.springframework.web.server.ResponseStatusException;
import tools.jackson.core.type.TypeReference;
import tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.TreeMap;

@Service
class ProductCatalog {

    record NewProduct(String sku, String name, String category, long sellerId, int pricePaise, Map<String, String> attributes) {
    }

    record Product(long id, String sku, String name, String category, long sellerId, int pricePaise, Map<String, String> attributes) {
    }

    private static final TypeReference<TreeMap<String, String>> MAP = new TypeReference<>() {
    };
    private static final String COLUMNS = "id, sku, name, category_code, seller_id, price_paise, attributes::text AS attributes";

    private final JdbcClient jdbc;
    private final AttributeRules rules;
    private final JsonMapper json;

    ProductCatalog(JdbcClient jdbc, AttributeRules rules, JsonMapper json) {
        this.jdbc = jdbc;
        this.rules = rules;
        this.json = json;
    }

    Product create(NewProduct p) {
        Map<String, AttributeRules.Rule> categoryRules = rules.of(p.category());
        if (categoryRules.isEmpty()) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "No category " + p.category());
        }
        Map<String, String> problems = rules.problems(categoryRules, p.attributes());
        if (!problems.isEmpty()) {
            ProblemDetail detail = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "These attributes do not fit a " + p.category() + " product");
            detail.setProperty("attributes", problems);
            throw new ErrorResponseException(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, detail, null);
        }
        try {
            long id = jdbc.sql("""
                            INSERT INTO products (sku, name, category_code, seller_id, price_paise, attributes)
                            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, CAST(? AS jsonb)) RETURNING id""")
                    .params(p.sku(), p.name(), p.category(), p.sellerId(), p.pricePaise(), json.writeValueAsString(p.attributes()))
                    .query(Long.class).single();
            return byId(id);
        } catch (DuplicateKeyException e) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.CONFLICT, "SKU " + p.sku() + " already exists");
        } catch (DataIntegrityViolationException e) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "No seller " + p.sellerId());   // the only other foreign key left
        }
    }

    Product byId(long id) {
        return jdbc.sql("SELECT " + COLUMNS + " FROM products WHERE id = ?").param(id).query((rs, i) -> new Product(rs.getLong("id"),
                rs.getString("sku"), rs.getString("name"), rs.getString("category_code"), rs.getLong("seller_id"), rs.getInt("price_paise"),
                json.readValue(rs.getString("attributes"), MAP))).single();
    }

    /** Containment (@>): "the attributes include all of these pairs", which the GIN index answers. */
    List<Product> search(String category, Map<String, String> wanted) {
        if (category != null && rules.of(category).isEmpty()) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "No category " + category);
        }
        List<String> known = (category == null ? jdbc.sql("SELECT DISTINCT name FROM attribute_definitions")
                : jdbc.sql("SELECT name FROM attribute_definitions WHERE category_code = ?").param(category)).query(String.class).list();
        wanted.keySet().stream().filter(name -> !known.contains(name)).findFirst().ifPresent(name -> {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "No attribute " + name + (category == null ? "" : " for " + category));
        });
        JdbcClient.StatementSpec query = jdbc.sql("SELECT " + COLUMNS + " FROM products WHERE attributes @> CAST(:wanted AS jsonb)"
                + (category == null ? "" : " AND category_code = :category") + " ORDER BY id LIMIT 50").param("wanted", json.writeValueAsString(wanted));
        if (category != null) {
            query = query.param("category", category);
        }
        return query.query((rs, i) -> new Product(rs.getLong("id"), rs.getString("sku"), rs.getString("name"), rs.getString("category_code"),
                        rs.getLong("seller_id"), rs.getInt("price_paise"), json.readValue(rs.getString("attributes"), MAP))).list();
    }
}

Why
Rules are rows, so a new category needs no code.
Without it

package com.kartwala.attributes;

import org.springframework.jdbc.core.simple.JdbcClient;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.sql.Array;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.TreeMap;

/** The attribute rules of a category, read from attribute_definitions, and the check a new product must pass. */
@Component
class AttributeRules {

    record Rule(String name, boolean required, List<String> allowed) {
    }

    private final JdbcClient jdbc;

    AttributeRules(JdbcClient jdbc) {
        this.jdbc = jdbc;
    }

    /** Name to rule, for one category; empty if the category does not exist. */
    Map<String, Rule> of(String category) {
        Map<String, Rule> rules = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        jdbc.sql("SELECT name, required, allowed FROM attribute_definitions WHERE category_code = ? ORDER BY name").param(category)
                .query((rs, i) -> {
                    Array allowed = rs.getArray("allowed");
                    return new Rule(rs.getString("name"), rs.getBoolean("required"), allowed == null ? null : Arrays.asList((String[]) allowed.getArray()));
                }).list().forEach(r -> rules.put(r.name(), r));
        return rules;
    }

    /** Every problem with these attributes, by attribute name; empty means valid. */
    Map<String, String> problems(Map<String, Rule> rules, Map<String, String> attributes) {
        Map<String, String> problems = new TreeMap<>();
        attributes.forEach((name, value) -> {
            Rule rule = rules.get(name);
            if (rule == null) {
                problems.put(name, "not an attribute of this category; known: " + rules.keySet());
            } else if (rule.allowed() != null && !rule.allowed().contains(value)) {
                problems.put(name, "must be one of " + rule.allowed());
            }
        });
        List<String> missing = new ArrayList<>();
        rules.values().stream().filter(r -> r.required() && !attributes.containsKey(r.name())).forEach(r -> missing.add(r.name()));
        missing.forEach(name -> problems.put(name, "is required"));
        return problems;
    }
}

Does
Columns with constraints, jsonb with a shape check, the GIN index, and the rules table.
Why
jsonb_path_ops is smaller and faster for @>, the one question asked.
Without it
A table that accepts anything.
CREATE TABLE sellers (
    id   BIGINT       PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE categories (
    code VARCHAR(30) PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL
);

-- What each category's attributes may be. Read by the app to validate; data, not code, so a new category needs no release.
CREATE TABLE attribute_definitions (
    category_code VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL CONSTRAINT attribute_definitions_category_fk REFERENCES categories (code),
    name          VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL CONSTRAINT attribute_definitions_name_shape CHECK (name ~ '^[a-z][a-z_]{1,29}$'),
    required      BOOLEAN     NOT NULL,
    allowed       TEXT[],      -- null: any text up to 40 characters
    CONSTRAINT attribute_definitions_pk PRIMARY KEY (category_code, name)
);

-- Fields every product has, that need a rule or a join, are columns. Only what differs per category is jsonb.
CREATE TABLE products (
    id            BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    sku           VARCHAR(30)  NOT NULL CONSTRAINT products_sku_unique UNIQUE,
    name          VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    category_code VARCHAR(30)  NOT NULL CONSTRAINT products_category_fk REFERENCES categories (code),
    seller_id     BIGINT       NOT NULL CONSTRAINT products_seller_fk REFERENCES sellers (id),
    price_paise   INTEGER      NOT NULL CONSTRAINT products_price_range CHECK (price_paise BETWEEN 100 AND 10000000),
    attributes    JSONB        NOT NULL CONSTRAINT products_attributes_object CHECK (jsonb_typeof(attributes) = 'object')
);
-- jsonb_path_ops: a smaller GIN index that answers containment (@>) only, which is the one question asked here.
CREATE INDEX products_attributes ON products USING GIN (attributes jsonb_path_ops);
CREATE INDEX products_category ON products (category_code);

class ProductDatabaseTest extends ApiTest {

        jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO products (sku, name, category_code, seller_id, price_paise, attributes) VALUES (?, 'Test', ?, ?, ?, CAST(? AS jsonb))")
                .params(sku, category, seller, paise, attributes).update();
    }

    @Test
    void namedConstraintsHoldWithoutJava() {
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> product("T-ARRAY", "phones", 7, 100000, "[\"8GB\"]")).isInstanceOf(DataAccessException.class).hasMessageContaining("products_attributes_object");
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> product("T-LAPTOP", "laptops", 7, 100000, "{}")).hasMessageContaining("products_category_fk");
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO attribute_definitions (category_code, name, required) VALUES ('phones', 'Battery Life', false)").update())
                .hasMessageContaining("attribute_definitions_name_shape");
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO attribute_definitions (category_code, name, required) VALUES ('phones', 'ram', false)").update())
                .hasMessageContaining("attribute_definitions_pk");
    }

    @Test
    void anUploadWithOneBadRowAddsNothing() {
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> transaction.executeWithoutResult(tx -> {
            product("T-ONE", "shoes", 8, 99900, "{\"size\": \"8\", \"colour\": \"Red\"}");
            product("T-TWO", "shoes", 8, 99900, "{\"size\": \"9\", \"colour\": \"Red\"}");
            product("T-THREE", "shoes", 9, 99900, "{\"size\": \"10\", \"colour\": \"Red\"}");
        })).hasMessageContaining("products_seller_fk");
        assertThat(jdbc.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM products WHERE sku LIKE 'T-%'").query(Long.class).single()).isZero();
    }

    @Test
    void jsonbStoresTheDocumentNormalised() {
        product("T-ORDER", "shoes", 8, 99900, "{\"size\": \"8\", \"colour\": \"Red\", \"colour\": \"Blue\"}");
        // Keys sorted by length then bytes, whitespace dropped, and the last duplicate key wins: jsonb is not the text you sent.
        assertThat(jdbc.sql("SELECT attributes::text FROM products WHERE sku = 'T-ORDER'").query(String.class).single())
                .isEqualTo("{\"size\": \"8\", \"colour\": \"Blue\"}");
    }
}

package com.kartwala.attributes;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.AfterEach;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.boot.webmvc.test.autoconfigure.AutoConfigureMockMvc;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Import;
import org.springframework.http.MediaType;
import org.springframework.jdbc.core.simple.JdbcClient;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.MockMvc;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.ResultActions;
import org.springframework.transaction.support.TransactionTemplate;
import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.post;

/** Shared setup: the whole app on a real PostgreSQL with 6 hand-written and 60,000 generated products. Test SKUs start with T- and are removed. */
@SpringBootTest
@AutoConfigureMockMvc
@Import(PostgresTestConfig.class)
abstract class ApiTest {

    @Autowired
    MockMvc mvc;
    @Autowired
    JdbcClient jdbc;
    @Autowired
    TransactionTemplate transaction;

    final JsonMapper json = JsonMapper.builder().build();

    @AfterEach
    void removeTestProducts() {
        jdbc.sql("DELETE FROM products WHERE sku LIKE 'T-%'").update();
    }

    ResultActions create(String body) throws Exception {
        return mvc.perform(post("/products").contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON).content(body));
    }

    /** Index names in the plan of a query, from EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON). */
    List<String> indexesUsed(String sql, Map<String, Object> params) {
        String plan = jdbc.sql("EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) " + sql).params(params).query(String.class).single();
        List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();
        collect(json.readTree(plan).get(0).get("Plan"), names);
        return names;
    }

    private static void collect(JsonNode node, List<String> names) {
        if (node.has("Index Name")) {
            names.add(node.get("Index Name").asString());
        }
        if (node.has("Plans")) {
            node.get("Plans").forEach(child -> collect(child, names));
        }
    }
}

package com.kartwala.attributes;

import org.springframework.dao.DataIntegrityViolationException;
import org.springframework.dao.DuplicateKeyException;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.jdbc.core.simple.JdbcClient;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;
import org.springframework.web.server.ResponseStatusException;
import tools.jackson.core.type.TypeReference;
import tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.TreeMap;

@Service
class ProductCatalog {

    record NewProduct(String sku, String name, String category, long sellerId, int pricePaise, Map<String, String> attributes) {
    }

    record Product(long id, String sku, String name, String category, long sellerId, int pricePaise, Map<String, String> attributes) {
    }

    private static final TypeReference<TreeMap<String, String>> MAP = new TypeReference<>() {
    };
    private static final String COLUMNS = "id, sku, name, category_code, seller_id, price_paise, attributes::text AS attributes";

    private final JdbcClient jdbc;
    private final AttributeRules rules;
    private final JsonMapper json;

    ProductCatalog(JdbcClient jdbc, AttributeRules rules, JsonMapper json) {
        this.jdbc = jdbc;
        this.rules = rules;
        this.json = json;
    }

    Product create(NewProduct p) {
        Map<String, AttributeRules.Rule> categoryRules = rules.of(p.category());
        if (categoryRules.isEmpty()) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "No category " + p.category());
        }
        Map<String, String> problems = rules.problems(categoryRules, p.attributes());
        if (!problems.isEmpty()) {
            ProblemDetail detail = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "These attributes do not fit a " + p.category() + " product");
            detail.setProperty("attributes", problems);
            throw new ErrorResponseException(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, detail, null);
        }
        try {
            long id = jdbc.sql("""
                            INSERT INTO products (sku, name, category_code, seller_id, price_paise, attributes)
                            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, CAST(? AS jsonb)) RETURNING id""")
                    .params(p.sku(), p.name(), p.category(), p.sellerId(), p.pricePaise(), json.writeValueAsString(p.attributes()))
                    .query(Long.class).single();
            return byId(id);
        } catch (DuplicateKeyException e) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.CONFLICT, "SKU " + p.sku() + " already exists");
        } catch (DataIntegrityViolationException e) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "No seller " + p.sellerId());   // the only other foreign key left
        }
    }

    Product byId(long id) {
        return jdbc.sql("SELECT " + COLUMNS + " FROM products WHERE id = ?").param(id).query((rs, i) -> new Product(rs.getLong("id"),
                rs.getString("sku"), rs.getString("name"), rs.getString("category_code"), rs.getLong("seller_id"), rs.getInt("price_paise"),
                json.readValue(rs.getString("attributes"), MAP))).single();
    }

    /** Challenge 1: the rules, for a form. */
    List<AttributeRules.Rule> rulesOf(String category) {
        List<AttributeRules.Rule> list = List.copyOf(rules.of(category).values());
        if (list.isEmpty()) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No category " + category);
        }
        return list;
    }

    /** Challenge 2: GROUP BY one attribute's value (->>), filtered with the same containment as the search. */
    Map<String, Long> facet(String category, String facet, Map<String, String> wanted) {
        if (!rules.of(category).containsKey(facet)) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "No attribute " + facet + " for " + category);
        }
        Map<String, Long> counts = new TreeMap<>();
        jdbc.sql("""
                        SELECT attributes->>:facet AS value, count(*) AS n FROM products
                        WHERE category_code = :category AND attributes @> CAST(:wanted AS jsonb) AND attributes->>:facet IS NOT NULL   -- not "attributes ? :facet": JDBC reads that ? as a placeholder
                        GROUP BY 1""")
                .param("facet", facet).param("category", category).param("wanted", json.writeValueAsString(wanted))
                .query((rs, i) -> counts.put(rs.getString("value"), rs.getLong("n"))).list();
        return counts;
    }

    /** Containment (@>): "the attributes include all of these pairs", which the GIN index answers. */
    List<Product> search(String category, Map<String, String> wanted) {
        if (category != null && rules.of(category).isEmpty()) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "No category " + category);
        }
        List<String> known = (category == null ? jdbc.sql("SELECT DISTINCT name FROM attribute_definitions")
                : jdbc.sql("SELECT name FROM attribute_definitions WHERE category_code = ?").param(category)).query(String.class).list();
        wanted.keySet().stream().filter(name -> !known.contains(name)).findFirst().ifPresent(name -> {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "No attribute " + name + (category == null ? "" : " for " + category));
        });
        JdbcClient.StatementSpec query = jdbc.sql("SELECT " + COLUMNS + " FROM products WHERE attributes @> CAST(:wanted AS jsonb)"
                + (category == null ? "" : " AND category_code = :category") + " ORDER BY id LIMIT 50").param("wanted", json.writeValueAsString(wanted));
        if (category != null) {
            query = query.param("category", category);
        }
        return query.query((rs, i) -> new Product(rs.getLong("id"), rs.getString("sku"), rs.getString("name"), rs.getString("category_code"),
                        rs.getLong("seller_id"), rs.getInt("price_paise"), json.readValue(rs.getString("attributes"), MAP))).list();
    }
}

    /** Demo limits: up to 20 attributes, values up to 40 characters, prices Rs 1 to Rs 1 lakh. */
    record NewProduct(@NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "[A-Za-z0-9-]{3,30}") String sku,
                      @NotBlank @Size(max = 120) String name,
                      @NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "[a-z]{2,30}") String category,
                      @NotNull Long sellerId,
                      @NotNull @Min(100) @Max(10_000_000) Integer pricePaise,
                      @NotNull @Size(max = 20) Map<@Pattern(regexp = "[a-z][a-z_]{1,29}") String, @NotBlank @Size(max = 40) String> attributes) {
    }

    private final ProductCatalog catalog;

    ProductController(ProductCatalog catalog) {
        this.catalog = catalog;
    }

    @PostMapping("/products")
    ResponseEntity<ProductCatalog.Product> create(@Valid @RequestBody NewProduct body) {
        ProductCatalog.Product created = catalog.create(new ProductCatalog.NewProduct(body.sku().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT), body.name().strip(),
                body.category(), body.sellerId(), body.pricePaise(), body.attributes()));
        return ResponseEntity.created(URI.create("/products/" + created.id())).body(created);
    }

    @GetMapping("/categories/{code}/attributes")
    List<AttributeRules.Rule> rules(@PathVariable String code) {
        return catalog.rulesOf(code);
    }

    @GetMapping("/products/facets")
    Map<String, Long> facets(@RequestParam String category, @RequestParam String facet, @RequestParam Map<String, String> params) {
        Map<String, String> wanted = new TreeMap<>();
        params.forEach((key, value) -> {
            if (key.startsWith("attr.")) {
                wanted.put(key.substring(5), value);
            }
        });
        return catalog.facet(category, facet, wanted);
    }

    /** ?category=phones&attr.ram=8GB&attr.storage=128GB: every attr.* pair must match. */
    @GetMapping("/products")
    List<ProductCatalog.Product> search(@RequestParam Map<String, String> params) {
        Map<String, String> wanted = new TreeMap<>();
        params.forEach((key, value) -> {
            if (key.startsWith("attr.")) {
                wanted.put(key.substring(5), value);
            } else if (!key.equals("category")) {
                throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "Unknown parameter " + key);
            }
        });
        if (wanted.isEmpty() || wanted.size() > 10) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "Give 1 to 10 attr.<name>=<value> filters");
        }
        return catalog.search(params.get("category"), wanted);
    }
}

                            INSERT INTO products (sku, name, category_code, seller_id, price_paise, attributes)
                            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, CAST(? AS jsonb)) RETURNING id""")
                    .params(p.sku(), p.name(), p.category(), p.sellerId(), p.pricePaise(), json.writeValueAsString(p.attributes()))
                    .query(Long.class).single();
            return byId(id);
        } catch (DuplicateKeyException e) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.CONFLICT, "SKU " + p.sku() + " already exists");
        } catch (DataIntegrityViolationException e) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "No seller " + p.sellerId());   // the only other foreign key left
        }
    }

    Product byId(long id) {
        return jdbc.sql("SELECT " + COLUMNS + " FROM products WHERE id = ?").param(id).query((rs, i) -> new Product(rs.getLong("id"),
                rs.getString("sku"), rs.getString("name"), rs.getString("category_code"), rs.getLong("seller_id"), rs.getInt("price_paise"),
                json.readValue(rs.getString("attributes"), MAP))).single();
    }

    /** Challenge 1: the rules, for a form. */
    List<AttributeRules.Rule> rulesOf(String category) {
        List<AttributeRules.Rule> list = List.copyOf(rules.of(category).values());
        if (list.isEmpty()) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No category " + category);
        }
        return list;
    }

    /** Challenge 2: GROUP BY one attribute's value (->>), filtered with the same containment as the search. */
    Map<String, Long> facet(String category, String facet, Map<String, String> wanted) {
        if (!rules.of(category).containsKey(facet)) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "No attribute " + facet + " for " + category);
        }
        Map<String, Long> counts = new TreeMap<>();
        jdbc.sql("""
                        SELECT attributes->>:facet AS value, count(*) AS n FROM products
                        WHERE category_code = :category AND attributes @> CAST(:wanted AS jsonb) AND attributes->>:facet IS NOT NULL   -- not "attributes ? :facet": JDBC reads that ? as a placeholder
                        GROUP BY 1""")
                .param("facet", facet).param("category", category).param("wanted", json.writeValueAsString(wanted))
                .query((rs, i) -> counts.put(rs.getString("value"), rs.getLong("n"))).list();
        return counts;
    }

    /** Containment (@>): "the attributes include all of these pairs", which the GIN index answers. */
    List<Product> search(String category, Map<String, String> wanted) {
        if (category != null && rules.of(category).isEmpty()) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "No category " + category);
        }
        List<String> known = (category == null ? jdbc.sql("SELECT DISTINCT name FROM attribute_definitions")
                : jdbc.sql("SELECT name FROM attribute_definitions WHERE category_code = ?").param(category)).query(String.class).list();
        wanted.keySet().stream().filter(name -> !known.contains(name)).findFirst().ifPresent(name -> {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "No attribute " + name + (category == null ? "" : " for " + category));
        });
        JdbcClient.StatementSpec query = jdbc.sql("SELECT " + COLUMNS + " FROM products WHERE attributes @> CAST(:wanted AS jsonb)"
                + (category == null ? "" : " AND category_code = :category") + " ORDER BY id LIMIT 50").param("wanted", json.writeValueAsString(wanted));
        if (category != null) {
            query = query.param("category", category);
        }
        return query.query((rs, i) -> new Product(rs.getLong("id"), rs.getString("sku"), rs.getString("name"), rs.getString("category_code"),
                        rs.getLong("seller_id"), rs.getInt("price_paise"), json.readValue(rs.getString("attributes"), MAP))).list();
    }
}

package com.kartwala.attributes;

import jakarta.validation.Valid;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Max;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Min;

import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Pattern;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Size;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;
import org.springframework.web.server.ResponseStatusException;

import java.net.URI;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.TreeMap;

@RestController
class ProductController {

    /** Demo limits: up to 20 attributes, values up to 40 characters, prices Rs 1 to Rs 1 lakh. */
    record NewProduct(@NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "[A-Za-z0-9-]{3,30}") String sku,
                      @NotBlank @Size(max = 120) String name,
                      @NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "[a-z]{2,30}") String category,
                      @NotNull Long sellerId,
                      @NotNull @Min(100) @Max(10_000_000) Integer pricePaise,
                      @NotNull @Size(max = 20) Map<@Pattern(regexp = "[a-z][a-z_]{1,29}") String, @NotBlank @Size(max = 40) String> attributes) {
    }

    private final ProductCatalog catalog;

    ProductController(ProductCatalog catalog) {
        this.catalog = catalog;
    }

    @PostMapping("/products")
    ResponseEntity<ProductCatalog.Product> create(@Valid @RequestBody NewProduct body) {
        ProductCatalog.Product created = catalog.create(new ProductCatalog.NewProduct(body.sku().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT), body.name().strip(),
                body.category(), body.sellerId(), body.pricePaise(), body.attributes()));
        return ResponseEntity.created(URI.create("/products/" + created.id())).body(created);
    }

    @GetMapping("/categories/{code}/attributes")
    List<AttributeRules.Rule> rules(@PathVariable String code) {
        return catalog.rulesOf(code);
    }

    @GetMapping("/products/facets")
    Map<String, Long> facets(@RequestParam String category, @RequestParam String facet, @RequestParam Map<String, String> params) {
        Map<String, String> wanted = new TreeMap<>();
        params.forEach((key, value) -> {
            if (key.startsWith("attr.")) {
                wanted.put(key.substring(5), value);
            }
        });
        return catalog.facet(category, facet, wanted);
    }

    /** ?category=phones&attr.ram=8GB&attr.storage=128GB: every attr.* pair must match. */
    @GetMapping("/products")
    List<ProductCatalog.Product> search(@RequestParam Map<String, String> params) {
        Map<String, String> wanted = new TreeMap<>();
        params.forEach((key, value) -> {
            if (key.startsWith("attr.")) {
                wanted.put(key.substring(5), value);
            } else if (!key.equals("category")) {
                throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "Unknown parameter " + key);
            }
        });
        if (wanted.isEmpty() || wanted.size() > 10) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "Give 1 to 10 attr.<name>=<value> filters");
        }
        return catalog.search(params.get("category"), wanted);
    }
}

Implementation approach

  1. Write the trap test: the all-jsonb table and what goes wrong with it.
  2. Split fields: columns for what every product has and needs rules or joins, jsonb for the rest.
  3. Put each category's rules in a table, and check attributes against them before saving.
  4. Search by containment, with a GIN index built for it.

Column or attribute?

QuestionYes → columnNo → attribute
Does every product have it?price, seller, SKURAM, size
Does it need a constraint?price range, unique SKUfree text like colour
Is it joined to another table?seller, categorystorage size
Is it summed, sorted or compared as a number?pricea size shown as text

ApproachWhat it costsVerdict
Columns for common fields + jsonb attributes + rules tableValidation in the app; text values.Chosen
One wide table with a column per attributeHundreds of nullable columns; a migration per category.The starting point
Everything in jsonbNo constraints, no joins, fragile casts.The trap
Entity-attribute-value rows (product_id, name, value)Flexible; every filter is a self-join; no types.Hard to query

Database design

ObjectWhatWhy
products_sku_unique, products_price_range, products_seller_fk, products_category_fkConstraints on columnsThe rules the old table could not hold.
products_attributes_objectCHECK jsonb_typeof(attributes) = 'object'No arrays or strings where an object belongs.
products_attributesGIN (attributes jsonb_path_ops)Containment searches.
attribute_definitionsPK (category, name), name shape CHECKThe rules, as data.
CREATE TABLE sellers (
    id   BIGINT       PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE categories (
    code VARCHAR(30) PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL
);

-- What each category's attributes may be. Read by the app to validate; data, not code, so a new category needs no release.
CREATE TABLE attribute_definitions (
    category_code VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL CONSTRAINT attribute_definitions_category_fk REFERENCES categories (code),
    name          VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL CONSTRAINT attribute_definitions_name_shape CHECK (name ~ '^[a-z][a-z_]{1,29}$'),
    required      BOOLEAN     NOT NULL,
    allowed       TEXT[],      -- null: any text up to 40 characters
    CONSTRAINT attribute_definitions_pk PRIMARY KEY (category_code, name)
);

-- Fields every product has, that need a rule or a join, are columns. Only what differs per category is jsonb.
CREATE TABLE products (
    id            BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    sku           VARCHAR(30)  NOT NULL CONSTRAINT products_sku_unique UNIQUE,
    name          VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    category_code VARCHAR(30)  NOT NULL CONSTRAINT products_category_fk REFERENCES categories (code),
    seller_id     BIGINT       NOT NULL CONSTRAINT products_seller_fk REFERENCES sellers (id),
    price_paise   INTEGER      NOT NULL CONSTRAINT products_price_range CHECK (price_paise BETWEEN 100 AND 10000000),
    attributes    JSONB        NOT NULL CONSTRAINT products_attributes_object CHECK (jsonb_typeof(attributes) = 'object')
);
-- jsonb_path_ops: a smaller GIN index that answers containment (@>) only, which is the one question asked here.
CREATE INDEX products_attributes ON products USING GIN (attributes jsonb_path_ops);
CREATE INDEX products_category ON products (category_code);

Changing rules
A new required attribute applies to new products only; existing rows do not change. Decide whether to backfill, or to require it only on edit.

Free-text attributes drift ("Blue", "blue", "Navy"). Use allowed lists wherever people filter.
Index size
A GIN index covers every key and value; watch its size and update cost on large, write-heavy tables.
Wide documents
jsonb values over about 2 kB are compressed and stored out of line (TOAST); keep attributes small.

Interview takeaways

json or jsonb?

jsonb: stored parsed, so it can be indexed and queried efficiently; json keeps the exact text, including key order and duplicates.

Which jsonb queries can a GIN index answer?

With jsonb_ops: containment (@>), key existence (?, ?|, ?&) and jsonpath; with jsonb_path_ops: containment and jsonpath only, with a smaller index.

When should a field be a column instead of jsonb?

When every row has it, it needs a constraint, it is joined, or it is computed with; jsonb cannot carry those rules.

How do you validate jsonb?

In the app, against rules (here a table per category); in the database, at least its shape with CHECK constraints.

What is the risk of casting a jsonb value in a query?

One row with an unexpected value makes the cast fail and the whole query fail for every user.
